first_impression.reaction: Googled 'notice of intended marriage' because I wanted the rule, not a sales pitch. The first paragraph gives me a date stamp, the one month to 18 month window and 'Without it, the marriage cannot go ahead.' That's the answer in two lines. Then there's a Concierge link in paragraph three before anything is proved, which put my guard up a bit. I jumped to the FAQ, then the witnessing and 'which paperwork applies' sections. Section number of the Act, a form revision date, links to the AG's department, the prescribed authority list and Smartraveller. All stuff I can check. It reads like a reference page with a planner attached at the end, which is how I'd want it.

journey.quote: As at November 2026, it must reach your celebrant at least one month and no more than 18 months before the day.
journey.reaction: Dated, specific, and the exact window I came for. Good.

journey.quote: When the legal route is settled, [Wedded Concierge](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=notice-of-intended-marriage&utm_content=primary) can take on the celebration.
journey.reaction: Sales link before the page has shown me anything. It's soft and conditional, so minor, but evidence first, then the ask.

journey.section: What is a Notice of Intended Marriage (NOIM)?
journey.quote: Section 42 of the Marriage Act 1961 says a marriage shall not be solemnised unless written notice of the intended marriage, on this form, is given to the authorised celebrant solemnising it.
journey.reaction: The actual section of the Act. I can look that up myself, and it checks out as a source.

journey.quote: For a couple who books a venue two summers ahead, that means the date is often secured long before the paperwork can begin.
journey.reaction: Makes sense as logic, but 'often' is a generalisation with nothing behind it. I'd discount it.

journey.quote: Treat that as a floor, not a target.
journey.reaction: Practical, and it's tied to the in-person meeting requirement, so it's not just opinion. That goes in the spreadsheet.

journey.quote: The form was last updated on 1 September 2021.
journey.reaction: A revision date. That's what lets me check I've got the right version. Small, but it tells me someone actually looked.

journey.section: Step 3: Sign in front of an authorised witness
journey.quote: The people who can act as authorised witnesses are listed on the form itself, in the section headed "Signatures of parties and witnesses".
journey.reaction: So the page on who can witness doesn't actually tell me who can witness. It sends me to the PDF. Honest about where the authority sits, but it's the one question I came with that I still have to answer somewhere else.

journey.quote: If you are outside Australia, your authorised witness must also be outside Australia, and cannot be a celebrant.
journey.reaction: That's the catch I'd have walked into: assuming my celebrant could just do it on Zoom. Flagged clearly, repeated where it matters.

journey.section: Lodging a NOIM when you live overseas
journey.quote: Many couples planning a wedding in Australia are living abroad when the paperwork starts.
journey.reaction: 'Many couples' according to whom? Unsourced filler in an otherwise sourced section.

journey.section: Can the one-month notice be shortened?
journey.quote: Approval is never automatic, so start with your celebrant and treat a shortening of time as a fallback, not a plan.
journey.reaction: Lists the actual grounds, who decides, links the list of authorities, then tells me not to rely on it. That's the trade-off stated honestly.

journey.section: Does the NOIM differ by state?
journey.quote: For any local step in the state or territory where you will marry, ask your celebrant.
journey.reaction: The answer is basically 'no, it's one form', which is fine, but the section ends on 'ask your celebrant' without saying what those local steps might be. Thin.

journey.quote: An Australian authorised celebrant cannot perform a marriage overseas, and an overseas marriage cannot be registered in Australia.
journey.reaction: Straight rule, no wiggle room. This is the bit that actually decides my plan.

journey.quote: DFAT can issue a CNI in Australia, but some local authorities accept only CNIs issued in their own country.
journey.reaction: Another trap pointed out before I waste time on it. Good.

journey.quote: A foreign marriage certificate is usually accepted as proof of the marriage, but you may not be able to use it for a name change, so check with your local registry.
journey.reaction: A limitation stated plainly, with who to ask. Not pretending it's all sorted.

journey.section: NOIM or marrying abroad: which paperwork applies?
journey.quote: Either way, the legal steps stay with you and your celebrant or the local authority.
journey.reaction: They're telling me what they don't do. A planner admitting a limit is worth more to me than a list of what they do.

journey.section: NOIM or marrying abroad: which paperwork applies?
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor is a single point of contact who plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments for the celebration abroad, works in your time zone and quotes in AUD, with the fee agreed in writing before any work begins;
journey.reaction: 'Fee agreed in writing before any work begins' is the right signal. Still doesn't tell me whether suppliers pay them a cut, but that's a call question.

journey.quote: Once the NOIM is with your celebrant, or your CNI is on its way, the rest is the part you will remember.
journey.reaction: Brochure voice at the end. Harmless, I skip it. The 'confirms the inclusions in writing' bit in the same paragraph is what I actually notice.

unanswered_questions: Who exactly can witness the NOIM? The page points to the list on the form but doesn't summarise it, so I still have to open the PDF.
If our wedding date moves after the NOIM is lodged, does the existing NOIM still stand or do we need a new one? The FAQ only says to keep the celebrant informed.
For the 'legal in Australia, celebrate abroad' route, does the Wedded Advisor help line up the dates of the two events, or is that entirely on us?
Does Wedded Wonderland take a commission or mark-up from venues or suppliers? (deferred business detail)
Is there a real wedding you've planned on the split route, legal at home and celebration abroad, with the actual budget?

turn_offs_found.quote: When the legal route is settled, [Wedded Concierge](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=notice-of-intended-marriage&utm_content=primary) can take on the celebration.
turn_offs_found.why: A CTA in the intro, before any evidence. It's conditional so it's minor, but I came for a government form and got a sales link before the facts.

turn_offs_found.quote: Many couples planning a wedding in Australia are living abroad when the paperwork starts.
turn_offs_found.why: 'Many couples' is an unsourced generalisation on a page that otherwise cites everything. It's the kind of line I discount and it makes me wonder what else is padding.

turn_offs_found.quote: For a couple who books a venue two summers ahead, that means the date is often secured long before the paperwork can begin.
turn_offs_found.why: 'Often' with nothing behind it. Probably true, but it's an assertion, not a fact.

turn_offs_found.quote: Once the NOIM is with your celebrant, or your CNI is on its way, the rest is the part you will remember.
turn_offs_found.why: Emotional sales copy instead of facts. It's the tone I skip.

would_share_with: My partner, the 'NOIM or marrying abroad: which paperwork applies?' section, because that's the decision we actually have to make
My partner, the overseas witnessing rule, since we'd assumed our celebrant could do it remotely

cta_reaction.why: The page earned some credit: it's sourced, dated, and it says plainly the legal side isn't theirs. 'Fee agreed in writing' and 'confirms the inclusions in writing' are the right words. But I came here for a form, not a planner, and my real question, whether they take a cut from suppliers, isn't answered. I'd bookmark them for the comparison spreadsheet rather than enquire off this page.

top_3_changes: Summarise who can witness a NOIM on the page, attributed to the form, instead of only pointing to it. 'The people who can act as authorised witnesses are listed on the form itself, in the section headed "Signatures of parties and witnesses".' leaves the most practical question unanswered.

Move the intro Concierge link below the key takeaways or into the 'which paperwork applies' section, so the facts come before the ask: 'When the legal route is settled, Wedded Concierge can take on the celebration.'

Cut or source the unsupported generalisations: 'Many couples planning a wedding in Australia are living abroad when the paperwork starts.' and 'the date is often secured long before the paperwork can begin.'
